The imported obstruction is covered by [Sherstov’s Theorem 1.10 and its disjunction extension](https://web.cs.ucla.edu/~sherstov/pdf/hshs.pdf); the inverse and conditional-selection arguments supply the required original-experiment achievability without an additional assumed statistical bound. Sample-size planning remains uncalibrated because the bounds have extremely loose constants, no relative Gaussian comparison, and no delivered implementation or numerical power analysis. proof_attempt_summary: Derived matched log-squared excess-power bounds throughout the full stated joint sample-size/gain window for the original six-cell Bernoulli experiment, including a bounded original-data Bernstein-envelope test, all-test converse, and exact onset certificates. D0.5 math and decision panels pass with no findings and all three cited inputs verified; the normalized tier is subfield with projected score 6.5 below the field threshold 7.4, and an independent terminal-validity consult finds no bounded same-scope repair. Formalization was not launched; the onset coefficient, interval between the priced window and cutoff, calibrated implementation, and broader constructive validity remain unresolved.
tldr: In the exact balanced two-stratum, three-arm Bernoulli trial, the causal value of personalization over the best common intervention is \(\Delta_n=G(h)/\sqrt n\). A computable finite count-table test has size at most \(1/10\) over the entire common-best-action null and achieves the same logarithmic excess-power order as the converse for every randomized full-record test: \(cL^2\le F_n(L)\le CL^2\) uniformly for \(L_0\le L\le10^{-5}n\). The finite experiment has a cutoff of order \(n\) in \(L\): positive excess holds below \(-\log\delta_n^+\), and excess is exactly zero at and above that cutoff, including the certified range \(L\ge2(n+1)/c_0+\log4\). The onset decreases with sample size. Its normalized logarithm has an interval of subsequential limits whose endpoints, and possible equality, remain open.
gap: Fixed-gain Gaussian convergence does not determine power improvements of size \(\exp[-O(L^2)]\) when \(L\) grows with \(n\).
fill: Combine full-comparison sign margins, a globally bounded damped count inverse, and an orthogonal original-record likelihood converse on the specified six-coordinate benchmark class.
